items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the biographical account 'The Making of a Scientist', and answer.

"When Meenal was nine, she noticed that the tulsi plant on the north window grew taller than the one on the south. She asked her teacher why. 'Find out,' the teacher said. So Meenal measured both every Sunday for six months, moved them around, watered one less than the other and kept a notebook full of tables. Her project did not win the district fair. It did, however, win her a lifelong habit of asking questions."

Answer the following:
(i) What did Meenal notice?
(ii) What did the teacher say?  (a) "It's magic."  (b) "Find out."  (c) "Don't worry."  (d) "Ask your mother."
(iii) How did Meenal investigate?
(iv) How is Meenal like Richard Ebright?
items.answer: (i) That the tulsi on the north window grew taller than the one on the south. (ii) (b) "Find out." (iii) By measuring both plants weekly, moving them, changing watering and recording tables. (iv) Both are curious, do real experiments and learn from science fairs.
items.markingKey: (i) That the tulsi on the north window grew taller than the one on the south. (ii) (b) "Find out." (iii) By measuring both plants weekly, moving them, changing watering and recording tables. (iv) Both are curious, do real experiments and learn from science fairs. (1 mark each, 4 marks.)
